clauses.reason: The only operative command of EO 8096 is its operative paragraph, which exempts William C. Shambaugh from compulsory retirement for age "for a period of one year ending August 31, 1940". The recital states the President's judgment that the public interest requires exempting William C. Shambaugh, who, during the month of August, 1939, "will reach the retirement age prescribed for automatic separation from the service". The command is a time-limited permission for one named employee, so it ended by its own terms on August 31, 1940; that date is recorded inclusive (the exemption runs through the end of that day), and the exclusive reading, under which it ends as that day begins, is the alternative a reviewer should see. EO 8414 (dated May 18, 1940 in its text) recites this order by number and further exempts the same employee "for a period of one year ending August 31, 1941"; it is recorded as a later event (a separate later exemption, an extension), not as the end of this order's command, which ended by its own stated period.

research_rationale:
EO 8096 (April 21, 1939) exempts William C. Shambaugh from compulsory retirement for age "for a period of one year ending August 31, 1940", under section 204 of the act of June 30, 1932 (47 Stat. 382, 404). I read the registered American Presidency Project transcription in full, confirmed its identity against the Common Crawl capture record (number, date, subject heading and text hash agree), and confirmed that it contains one operative command. The clause ended by its own stated period on August 31, 1940, recorded inclusive with the exclusive reading disclosed. Later extension orders are recorded as later events and do not end this order's clause. The text is a transcription (grade mirror_transcription) and the original is not yet held; replace and re-check quotes when an official copy is retrieved.

savings.reason: The order grants one named employee a permission to remain in service despite the retirement-age rule for a stated period and contains no savings, transition or continuing-obligation clause. Service the employee performed while the exemption was in force is a completed effect that does not depend on the order remaining in force, and no held source shows any other residual effect; it is recorded as accrued.
